findings.highlight: It’s daybreak.
findings.evidenceJa: 夜が明けようとしていた。
findings.governingReading: The night was about to give way to dawn.
findings.explanation: The English again advances the scene from impending dawn to daybreak already having arrived.

findings.highlight: I, Emiya Shirou, must fight that man when we get to the castle.
findings.evidenceJa: この森を抜けた時、衛宮士郎はその男と対決しなくてはならない。
findings.governingReading: When they emerge from this forest, Emiya Shirou must confront that man.
findings.explanation: The destination is changed from clearing the forest to reaching the castle.

findings.highlight: I know I’ll just be killed once we start fighting.
findings.evidenceJa: ひとたび剣を合わせれば、無惨に殺されるだけだという事も判っている。
findings.governingReading: He knows that once their swords cross, he will only be killed miserably or gruesomely.
findings.explanation: The concrete sword clash and the pitiful or gruesome quality of the expected death disappear.

findings.highlight: I’m not scared, but it’s not because I’m prepared for it.
findings.evidenceJa: 恐れがないのは、開き直ったからでも覚悟したからでもない。
findings.governingReading: His lack of fear comes from neither defiant resignation nor steeling himself for death.
findings.explanation: One half of the explicit double denial disappears, weakening the explanation of Shirou’s state.

findings.highlight: That being the case, I have no reason to worry.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな身分で、自身の死をどうだのと憂いる余裕などないだけだ。
findings.governingReading: In that condition, he simply has no room to concern himself with his own death.
findings.explanation: Lack of mental leeway becomes lack of a reason, and the object—his own death—is omitted.

findings.highlight: No matter who gets killed and who survives, the one to be eliminated is the same.
findings.evidenceJa: どちらが生きどちらが敗れようと、消える者は同じだ。
findings.governingReading: Whichever one lives and whichever one is defeated, the person who disappears is the same.
findings.explanation: The English replaces defeat with killing and reverses the paired ordering, hardening the duel’s outcome.

findings.highlight: Her desire to stop this ridiculous fight is causing her pain.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな馬鹿げた戦いを、彼女は今でも止めるべきだと苦悩している。
findings.governingReading: Even now, she agonizes over whether she ought to stop such an absurd battle.
findings.explanation: Saber’s continuing moral deliberation becomes a settled desire.

findings.highlight: The man is standing at the top of the stairs which are lit by the morning sun.
findings.evidenceJa: 崩れた階段の上、朝日差す踊り場に、その男の姿があった。
findings.governingReading: The man stands on the sunlit landing above the ruined staircase.
findings.explanation: The collapsed condition of the stairs and the distinct landing are erased.

findings.highlight: His red outfit is far away
findings.evidenceJa: 赤い外套は遠く
findings.governingReading: The red cloak is distant
findings.explanation: Archer’s identifying red cloak becomes generic clothing.

findings.highlight: his figure is hazy in the white glare.
findings.evidenceJa: 男の姿は白い情景に霞んでいる。
findings.governingReading: The man’s figure is veiled in the white scene or landscape.
findings.explanation: The surrounding white morning scene becomes optical glare.

findings.highlight: has many Noble Phantasms, yet carelessly destroys them
findings.evidenceJa: 多くの宝具を持ち、惜しげもなくそれらを散らしていった
findings.governingReading: possesses many Noble Phantasms and scatters or expends them without stint
findings.explanation: Archer’s lavish willingness to expend copied weapons becomes careless destruction.

findings.highlight: It is when the heroic spirit has a catalyst connected to the summoner.
findings.evidenceJa: 召喚者ではなく、呼び出された英霊そのものが、召喚者に縁のある触媒を持っていた場合のみだ
findings.governingReading: Only when the summoned Heroic Spirit itself, rather than the summoner, possesses a catalyst tied to the summoner.
findings.explanation: The English drops both the exclusive “only” and the emphasized reversal from summoner to summoned spirit.

findings.highlight: The knight in redArcher looks down at me from the top of the stairs.
findings.evidenceJa: 赤い外套の騎士アーチャーは階段からオレを見下ろしている。
findings.governingReading: The red-cloaked knight, Archer, looks down at me from the stairs.
findings.explanation: Missing separation fuses “red” and “Archer” into visible typographic debris.

findings.highlight: He is standing alone in this vast hall.
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツは一人きりで、この大広間に立っている。
findings.governingReading: He stands alone in the great hall.
findings.explanation: “Vast” adds an unsupported scale judgment to the location.

findings.highlight: He might not be able to restrain himself if she provokes him, so he might be killing and raping her doing something unnatural right now.
findings.evidenceJa: 凛に挑発された小僧は我慢できずに口火を切り、今頃は妙な事になっているかもしれんぞ
findings.governingReading: Provoked by Rin, the boy may have lost control and set things off; by now matters may have taken a strange turn.
findings.explanation: mirror moon invents explicit killing and rape where Archer gives a provocative but nonspecific possibility.

findings.highlight: if she provokes him
findings.evidenceJa: 凛に挑発された小僧は我慢できずに口火を切り
findings.governingReading: The boy, having been provoked by Rin, may have lost patience and fired the opening shot.
findings.explanation: A completed provocation and possible ensuing action become a future condition.

findings.highlight: killing and raping her doing something unnatural
findings.evidenceJa: 妙な事になっているかもしれんぞ
findings.governingReading: 妙な事 is a single vague predicate; a finished English line must choose a coherent rendering.
findings.explanation: Competing explicit and vague renderings remain spliced together as malformed English.

findings.highlight: I get pissed off.
findings.evidenceJa: 冷めていた頭に血が上る。
findings.governingReading: Blood rushes to his previously cool head.
findings.explanation: A physical image marking the loss of cold composure becomes a flat profanity.

findings.highlight: My entire reason for joining you was to keep that girl from dying.
findings.evidenceJa: もとから、オレはあのお嬢ちゃんを死なせない為に協力したワケだ。
findings.governingReading: From the outset, I cooperated in order to keep that young lady from dying.
findings.explanation: Cooperation in the immediate plan becomes joining Shirou, and “entire reason” overstates the source.

findings.highlight: this was rather comfortable.
findings.evidenceJa: これが思いの他居心地良くてな。
findings.governingReading: This proved more congenial or comfortable than expected.
findings.explanation: The contrast with Lancer’s expectations is omitted.

findings.highlight: With those words
findings.evidenceJa: そう軽口を叩きながら
findings.governingReading: Bantering lightly as he says this
findings.explanation: Lancer’s breezy, joking delivery disappears.

findings.highlight: I’m doing this out of my own interest.
findings.evidenceJa: これはあくまで俺の趣味だ。
findings.governingReading: This is strictly my own taste, whim, or personal inclination.
findings.explanation: Lancer frames the rescue as a freely chosen personal indulgence; “interest” weakens that claim of voluntary taste.

findings.highlight: I’ll at least follow through on this.
findings.evidenceJa: この命令は最後まで守り抜く。
findings.governingReading: I will carry this order through to the very end.
findings.explanation: The unsupported “at least” makes Lancer’s firm pledge sound like a minimum concession.

findings.highlight: You can concentrate on your own affairs.
findings.evidenceJa: そっちはそっちで、自分の面倒だけみてやがれ
findings.governingReading: You handle your side and look after yourself alone.
findings.explanation: Lancer’s blunt order that Shirou protect himself becomes vague attention to his affairs.

findings.highlight: He lightheartedly replies with a “yes”.
findings.evidenceJa: あいよ、と気軽に声を返す。
findings.governingReading: “Sure,” he answers lightly.
findings.explanation: Lancer’s casual, characterful assent becomes a stiff reported “yes.”

findings.highlight: He easily jumps up to the terrace and disappears into the passageway.
findings.evidenceJa: 青い槍兵は事も無げに二階のテラスへ跳躍し、振り返りもせず通路へと消えていった。
findings.governingReading: The blue spearman leaps effortlessly to the second-floor terrace and vanishes down the passage without looking back.
findings.explanation: The identifying blue-spearman image, second-floor position, and refusal to look back are omitted.

findings.highlight: It’s as if he’s saying Tohsaka is useless now.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂はもう用のない人間だと言うかのように。
findings.governingReading: As though saying Tohsaka is someone he no longer has any use for.
findings.explanation: Archer’s personal instrumental abandonment becomes an assertion that Rin herself is useless.

findings.highlight: I’ll have broken my contract with Rin for nothing.
findings.evidenceJa: 凛と契約を切った意味がない
findings.governingReading: There would have been no point in severing my contract with Rin.
findings.explanation: Archer’s deliberate termination of the contract becomes an accidental breach of it.

findings.highlight: Saber takes a quick breath
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女はわずかに息を呑み
findings.governingReading: She catches her breath slightly
findings.explanation: A small involuntary catch of breath becomes a quick breath.

findings.highlight: She finishes in a broken voice, “Why are you so different?”
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は、言葉にしない声で、吐き出した。
findings.governingReading: She expels the question in a voice that never becomes words.
findings.explanation: An explicitly unspoken question is presented as audible quoted dialogue.

findings.highlight: we would not be fighting here.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺もヤツも、ここで決着をつけようとは思わない。
findings.governingReading: Neither he nor I would be trying to settle matters here.
findings.explanation: The shared intention to reach a final settlement is reduced to the surface fact of fighting.

findings.highlight: then at Archer.
findings.evidenceJa: 広間に降りようとするアーチャーを見つめた。
findings.governingReading: then looks at Archer as he is about to descend into the hall.
findings.explanation: Archer’s continued descent and spatial movement are omitted.

findings.highlight: Maybe something she said got through to him.
findings.evidenceJa: それに何か感じ入るモノがあったのか。
findings.governingReading: Perhaps something in that moved or struck him.
findings.explanation: The English suggests Saber’s argument persuaded Archer instead of merely stirring a reaction.

findings.highlight: I became a superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方になったんだ
findings.governingReading: I became an ally or champion of justice
findings.explanation: The recurring ideal-name is again replaced by the culturally and tonally different “superhero.”

findings.highlight: someone who can save everyone
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる人を平等に救えるだろう
findings.governingReading: someone capable of saving every person equally
findings.explanation: The equality built into Shirou’s imagined rescue ideal disappears.

findings.highlight: I have saved the world from danger several times.
findings.evidenceJa: 世界の危機とやらを救った事もあったよ。
findings.governingReading: There were even occasions when I saved it from what they called a crisis of the world.
findings.explanation: The English invents the definite frequency “several times” and weakens the distancing phrase “what they call.”

findings.highlight: I did reach the place I had dreamed of for so long.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠い昔から憧れていた地位にさえ、ついには辿り着いた事もある
findings.governingReading: I finally even attained the status I had admired since long ago: hero.
findings.explanation: A specifically coveted social status becomes a generic place.

findings.highlight: You became a herothen Shirou was rewarded, right…?
findings.evidenceJa: 英雄に辿り着いたなら、シロウは報われたのですね
findings.governingReading: If you attained herohood, then Shirou was rewarded, wasn’t he?
findings.explanation: Missing separation fuses “hero” and “then” in a central emotional appeal.

findings.highlight: Shirou was able to make his wish come true.
findings.evidenceJa: シロウはちゃんと、その理想を叶えたのだから
findings.governingReading: Shirou properly fulfilled that ideal.
findings.explanation: The defined ethical ideal is generalized into a wish.

findings.highlight: There’s no conviction in her voice.
findings.evidenceJa: 訴える声に力はない。
findings.governingReading: Her pleading voice has no strength.
findings.explanation: Physical and emotional weakness in Saber’s plea becomes lack of belief or conviction.

findings.highlight: I killed so many that I stopped caring about innocent people
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人間の命なぞどうでもよくなるくらい殺して
findings.governingReading: I killed until even the lives of people unrelated to the immediate cause ceased to matter to me
findings.explanation: “Unrelated” becomes the morally stronger “innocent,” changing Archer’s description of widening collateral sacrifice.

findings.highlight: there are always people who will perish.
findings.evidenceJa: 救われない人間というモノは出てきてしまう。
findings.governingReading: There will inevitably be people who are not saved.
findings.explanation: Failure to save becomes death, making Archer’s claim categorically harsher.

findings.highlight: recounts his past.
findings.evidenceJa: かつての己を告白する。
findings.governingReading: confesses his former self
findings.explanation: The narration’s self-directed confessional framing is reduced to recounting events.

findings.highlight: I killed scores of people
findings.evidenceJa: 何十という人間の救いを殺して
findings.governingReading: I killed the salvation of dozens of people
findings.explanation: A deliberate metaphor about destroying people’s prospects of salvation becomes additional literal homicide.

findings.highlight: that everyone would become happy
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ誰も悲しまないだろう
findings.governingReading: that this time no one would grieve
findings.explanation: The limited hope of preventing sorrow is strengthened into making everyone happy.

findings.highlight: I just wanted people in my view not to cry.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が知りうるかぎりの世界では、誰にも涙して欲しくなかった
findings.governingReading: I only wanted no one to shed tears within the world as far as I could know it.
findings.explanation: The expanding world within Archer’s possible knowledge is narrowed to people currently in his visual field.

findings.highlight: Definitely my own wish.
findings.evidenceJa: 紛れもなく、衛宮士郎の願いのカタチ
findings.governingReading: Unmistakably the form or shape of Emiya Shirou’s wish.
findings.explanation: The English drops the predication that Archer’s confession embodies the shape of Shirou’s wish.

findings.highlight: I assume it was a daily routine for you to sacrifice a few people to save the country.
findings.evidenceJa: 国を救う為にほんの少しの人間を見殺しにする、なんていうのは日常茶飯事だっただろう？
findings.governingReading: Letting a small number die to save the country was routine for you, was it not?
findings.explanation: Archer’s pointed appeal to Saber’s known experience is softened into his assumption, while letting die becomes active sacrifice.

findings.highlight: The quiet voice is rendered powerless to object.
findings.evidenceJa: 押し黙る声は、反論する意思を奪われていた。
findings.governingReading: Her fallen-silent voice had been robbed of the will to object.
findings.explanation: The paradoxical image of a voice struck silent becomes an awkward passive construction about a quiet voice being rendered powerless.

findings.highlight: There are always fewer seats called happiness than there are people to fill them.
findings.evidenceJa: 幸福という椅子は、常に全体の数より少な目でしか用意されない。
findings.governingReading: The chairs called happiness are always prepared in a number smaller than the whole.
findings.explanation: The English supplies people specifically as the comparator, narrowing the deliberately general allocation metaphor.

findings.highlight: I quickly killed the ones that would eventually fall out
findings.evidenceJa: いずれこぼれる人間を速やかに、一秒でも早くこの手で切り落とした。
findings.governingReading: With my own hand, I swiftly cut away those who would eventually spill out, even one second sooner.
findings.explanation: The surgical allocation image, Archer’s own hand, and the obsessive one-second urgency collapse into generic quick killing.

findings.highlight: This is what it means to be that boy’s vision of the ideal superhero.
findings.evidenceJa: それが英雄と、その男が理想と信じる正義の味方の取るべき行動だ
findings.governingReading: That is the action a hero—and the ally of justice that man believes ideal—ought to take.
findings.explanation: An asserted rule of action becomes a malformed definition of being a superhero.

findings.highlight: The desire to save as many people as possible.
findings.evidenceJa: 出来るだけ多くの人間を救うという理想。
findings.governingReading: The ideal of saving as many people as possible.
findings.explanation: The defined ethical ideal is reduced to a desire.

findings.highlight: The only people a superhero can save are the people he sides with.
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方が助けられるのは、味方をした人間だけ。
findings.governingReading: An ally of justice can save only those whose side he takes.
findings.explanation: The central wordplay and ideal-name built on 味方 is replaced by “superhero.”

findings.highlight: I killed one to save many.
findings.evidenceJa: 大勢の為に一人には死んで貰った。
findings.governingReading: For the sake of the many, I had one person die.
findings.explanation: The source’s coercive but indirect allocation formula becomes a direct claim of personally killing the one.

findings.highlight: quickly killed the people who opposed me.
findings.evidenceJa: 敵対した者は速やかに皆殺しにした。
findings.governingReading: I swiftly slaughtered every person who opposed me.
findings.explanation: The total scope and the force of slaughtering them all are weakened.

findings.highlight: Don’t you think such a guy should die?
findings.evidenceJa: そんな男は、今のうちに死んだ方が世の為と思わないか？
findings.governingReading: Do you not think the world would be better served if such a man died now, while there is still time?
findings.explanation: Archer’s claimed benefit to the world and urgency are omitted.

findings.highlight: A frown crosses his face.
findings.evidenceJa:
ヤツは、わずか。
一度だけ、苦々しげに眉を曇らせた。
findings.governingReading: For the briefest instant—only once—his brow clouds bitterly.
findings.explanation: The uniquely brief crack in Archer’s composure becomes a generic frown.

findings.highlight:
He starts laughing like a madman.
…As if it’s the funniest thing he’s heard.
findings.evidenceJa:
心底おかしい、と。
はじけるように、笑い出した。
findings.governingReading: Finding it funny from the bottom of his heart, he bursts into laughter.
findings.explanation: mirror moon invents madness and reverses the source’s explicit description of genuine amusement into an appearance.

findings.highlight: Wow, that is great.
findings.evidenceJa: いや、これは傑作だ。
findings.governingReading: No, this is a masterpiece.
findings.explanation: Archer’s cutting theatrical appraisal is flattened into generic approval.

findings.highlight: nor have I forced such a meaningless concept on anyone.
findings.evidenceJa: 他の誰にも、そんな無責任なモノを押しつけた覚えはない
findings.governingReading: I have no memory of foisting such an irresponsible thing on anyone else.
findings.explanation: The charge that imposing guilt would be irresponsible becomes a claim that guilt is meaningless.

findings.highlight: The knight looks completely calm. calmly goes mad.
findings.evidenceJa: 騎士は、あくまで冷静に見える。
findings.governingReading: The knight appears calm throughout.
findings.explanation: mirror moon appends “calmly goes mad,” unsupported English debris that contradicts the source and its own preceding sentence.

findings.highlight: was executed in the end.
findings.evidenceJa: 最後には絞首台だ。
findings.governingReading: and in the end, the gallows.
findings.explanation: Archer’s concrete death on the gallows becomes generic execution.

findings.highlight: “Whatimpossible, Archer. You cannot mean your end is…”
findings.evidenceJa: 「なうそだ、アーチャー。貴方の、最期は」
findings.governingReading: “No… that cannot be true, Archer. Your end was…”
findings.explanation: The English fuses two reaction words into the visible error “Whatimpossible.”

findings.highlight: people who become guardians are removed from the circle of reincarnation
findings.evidenceJa: 己が存在を守護者に預けたモノは輪廻の枠から外れ
findings.governingReading: those who entrust their existence to the role of Guardian are removed from the cycle of reincarnation
findings.explanation: A contractual surrender of one’s existence becomes the generic act of becoming a Guardian.

findings.highlight: SoI thought it would be fine
findings.evidenceJa: なら守護者となって
findings.governingReading: So I thought it would be enough to become a Guardian
findings.explanation: A missing space visibly fuses “So” and “I.”

findings.highlight: harmful people
findings.evidenceJa: 世界に害を与えるであろう人々
findings.governingReading: people who are expected to pose a danger to the world
findings.explanation: A prospective risk judgment becomes an inherent label of harmfulness.

findings.highlight: others who are enjoying life
findings.evidenceJa: 絶望と無関係に生を謳歌する部外者
findings.governingReading: outsiders who enjoy life untouched by that despair
findings.explanation: The crucial fact that the protected people are outsiders unrelated to the sufferers’ despair is omitted.

findings.highlight: You have repeated such a thing forever
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方は、ずっと、そんな事を
findings.governingReading: You have been doing that all this time
findings.explanation: Saber’s horrified question about Archer’s long condition becomes a literal claim of eternal repetition.

findings.highlight: The strong feed on the weak
findings.evidenceJa: 強者が弱者を奪い尽くす
findings.governingReading: the strong strip the weak of everything
findings.explanation: Complete dispossession becomes a different predatory metaphor.

findings.highlight: take care of the crime people have created
findings.evidenceJa: 人間が作ってしまった罪の後始末
findings.governingReading: clean up the sins humanity has brought into being
findings.explanation: Plural, cumulative human wrongdoing becomes a single definite crime.

findings.highlight: A being that repairs the damage caused by human desire.
findings.evidenceJa: 人間が生み出した欲望を消す為だけの存在。
findings.governingReading: A being that exists only to erase the desires produced by humanity.
findings.explanation: Erasing desire itself becomes the more benign task of repairing consequential damage.

findings.highlight: he saw people nearly destroy themselves through their own actions, and he burned them down like trash each time.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの手で滅びようとする人間の業を目の当たりにし、それを、ゴミのように焼き払ってきた。
findings.governingReading: He witnessed human karma bent on self-destruction and burned that karma away like refuse.
findings.explanation: The object burned shifts from humanity’s destructive karma or deeds to the people themselves.

findings.highlight: The man became a hero with that one wishbut in the end
findings.evidenceJa: その思いだけで英雄になった男は
findings.governingReading: The man who became a hero on that conviction alone, in the end
findings.explanation: A missing space fuses “wish” and “but” in the sentence.

findings.highlight: a worn-out corpse.
findings.evidenceJa: とうに摩耗しきった残骸だった。
findings.governingReading: the wreckage left after being worn away completely long ago.
findings.explanation: The metaphorical remnant of Archer’s eroded self becomes a literal corpse.

findings.highlight: Save one exception.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ一つの例外を除いて
findings.governingReading: Except for one single exception.
findings.explanation: The exception clause is rendered in conspicuously archaic, misleading English.

findings.highlight: There is only one objective for Archer: to kill his own self.
findings.evidenceJa: アーチャーの目的はただ一つ、自身の消去だ。
findings.governingReading: Archer has only one objective: his own erasure.
findings.explanation: The metaphysical objective of erasing his existence becomes merely killing himself.

findings.highlight: the real body of Emiya, who is in the “place” outside of the cycle
findings.evidenceJa: 輪の外にある“座”に在るエミヤ本体
findings.governingReading: Emiya’s original or main existence in the “Throne” outside the cycle
findings.explanation: The technical Throne and the distinction between manifested Archer and the original Emiya are flattened into a body located in a generic place.

findings.highlight: something that is not part of the real world
findings.evidenceJa: この世界の輪に無いモノ
findings.governingReading: something outside this world’s cycle
findings.explanation: The cosmological cycle is replaced by a reality-versus-unreality distinction.

findings.highlight: I could not contain myself unless I believed in it.
findings.evidenceJa: そう思わなければ自身を許容できなかった。
findings.governingReading: Without believing that, I could not accept or tolerate my own existence.
findings.explanation: Archer’s inability to accept himself becomes inability to control himself.

findings.highlight: If the distortion is large enougha hero called Emiya
findings.evidenceJa: 歪みが大きければ、或いはここで
findings.governingReading: If the distortion is great enough, perhaps the hero called Emiya
findings.explanation: Missing punctuation and spacing fuse “enough” to the following clause.

findings.highlight: you should not have become a superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方になぞなるべきではなかった
findings.governingReading: you should never have become an ally of justice
findings.explanation: The core ideal-name is again changed to “superhero.”

findings.highlight: I’ll destroy such an incorrect ideal with my own hands.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな間違った理想は、俺自身の手でたたき出す
findings.governingReading: I will beat that mistaken ideal out with my own hands.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s bodily, confrontational phrasing is generalized to destruction.

findings.highlight: I’ve always believed that I am right.
findings.evidenceJa: それを正しいと信じてここまできた。
findings.governingReading: I came this far believing that way of living was right.
findings.explanation: Belief in the rightness of his chosen conduct becomes a broader assertion of personal infallibility.

findings.highlight: The simple twin swords I admired
findings.evidenceJa: 見惚れた無骨な双剣。
findings.governingReading: the rugged, unadorned twin swords that captivated me
findings.explanation: The swords’ austere ruggedness and Shirou’s captivated gaze are weakened to simplicity and admiration.

findings.highlight: are too unprecise
findings.evidenceJa: あまりにも曖昧だ。
findings.governingReading: are far too vague or indistinct
findings.explanation: mirror moon uses the nonstandard “unprecise” and fails to express the projection’s indistinct construction.

findings.highlight: will shatter and disappear
findings.evidenceJa: 無惨に砕け散るだろう。
findings.governingReading: will shatter miserably into fragments
findings.explanation: Scattering into shattered pieces becomes disappearance.

findings.highlight:
Crunch.
The rubble crunches under my foot.
findings.evidenceJa:
きちり、と。
踏み込んだ足元で、瓦礫が軋む音がする。
findings.governingReading: A sharp creak: the rubble strains beneath the planted foot.
findings.explanation: The distinct creaking or straining sound is replaced by two generic crunches.

findings.highlight: That serves as the signal.
findings.evidenceJa: それが開始の合図になったのか。
findings.governingReading: Perhaps that became the signal to begin.
findings.explanation: A narrator’s tentative question is promoted into fact.

findings.highlight: The opposing swords
findings.evidenceJa: 一対の武装、四つの刃は
findings.governingReading: The paired weapons—their four blades—
findings.explanation: The exact paired construction and count of four blades are omitted.

findings.highlight: They are drawn together like magnets and clash into each other.
findings.evidenceJa: 磁力で引き合ったように重なり、弾け合った。
findings.governingReading: As though magnetically attracted, they overlap and then spring violently apart.
findings.explanation: The two-stage motion of meeting and repelling is collapsed into a generic clash.
